sources.title: Chamber of Commerce of the State of New York, Rapid Transit in New York City and in the Other Great Cities (1906), ch. 4 "Bridges to Brooklyn"

towerHeightM.note: height (P2048): tower top above the water. (The 1906 text gives the 400 ft of the design then; the towers were built lower.)

mainSpanM.note: main span (P2787); the 1906 text gives 1,470 ft between tower centres

totalLengthM.note: length (P2043). The game fits the bridge to its LION frame (spanM).

deckWidthM.note: width (P2049); the 1906 text gives the floor as 120 ft wide over all

midspanClearanceM.note: vertical clearance (P2793): the deck top at mid-span

sideSpanM.note: "each land span will be 725 feet in length"

mainCables.note: four cables (the 1906 text specifies cables and suspenders); diameter estimated

trussDepthM.note: the deep stiffening trusses that carry the double deck, proportioned by eye

towerLeg.note: each steel tower leg's section, proportioned from the tower height

towerPier.note: the masonry pier each tower stands on, wider than the deck

pierTopM.note: the masonry pier's top above the water

crownM.note: the depth of the crown girder and finials at the top of each tower

anchorage.note: stylised anchorage blocks sized to take the cables; mostly hidden under the game's land top

readabilityScale.note: Thin members are drawn this many times their true width so they read at game distance; suspenders are drawn sparser than the real ones.

gameScale.note: Game scale (orchestrator decision 2026-10-08, the user may overrule): heights x1.8 and widths x1.6 against the real numbers above (1.6, not 2, keeps the 59 m deck inside the frame's 64 m exclusion), so the bridge reads at the 3,000-4,500 m game camera. Lengths along the axis stay real.
